title: Architects, Except Landscape and Naval
description: Plan and design structures, such as private residences, office buildings, theaters, factories, and other structural property.
tasks: Develop final construction plans that include aesthetic representations of the structure or details for its construction.
Prepare scale drawings or architectural designs, using computer-aided design or other tools.
Prepare information regarding design, structure specifications, materials, color, equipment, estimated costs, or construction time.
Consult with clients to determine functional or spatial requirements of structures.
Meet with clients to review or discuss architectural drawings.
Monitor the work of specialists, such as electrical engineers, mechanical engineers, interior designers, or sound specialists to ensure optimal form or function of designs or final structures.
Integrate engineering elements into unified architectural designs.
Plan layouts of structural architectural projects.
Conduct periodic on-site observations of construction work to monitor compliance with plans.
Prepare contract documents for building contractors.
Plan or design structures such as residences, office buildings, theatres, factories, or other structural properties in accordance with environmental, safety, or other regulations.
Direct activities of technicians engaged in preparing drawings or specification documents.
Administer construction contracts.
Create three-dimensional or interactive representations of designs, using computer-assisted design software.
Represent clients in obtaining bids or awarding construction contracts.
Develop marketing materials, proposals, or presentations to generate new work opportunities.
Perform predesign services, such as feasibility or environmental impact studies.
Design structures that incorporate environmentally friendly building practices or concepts, such as Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) standards.
Design or plan construction of green building projects to minimize adverse environmental impact or conserve energy.
Gather information related to projects' environmental sustainability or operational efficiency.
Inspect proposed building sites to determine suitability for construction.
Design environmentally sound structural upgrades to existing buildings, such as natural lighting systems, green roofs, or rainwater collection systems.
Calculate potential energy savings by comparing estimated energy consumption of proposed design to baseline standards.
Prepare operating and maintenance manuals, studies, or reports.

role_contexts.Indoors, Environmentally Controlled: Once a week or more but not every day

psychological_profile.core_drive: The need to impose conceptual order on physical chaos—to see a coherent vision where others see only fragmented constraints and materials.
psychological_profile.decision_style: Under pressure, they default to rapid aesthetic judgment over exhaustive analysis, trusting that formal elegance will resolve functional problems later; when time permits, they gather excessive stakeholder input to diffuse responsibility for controversial choices.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They immediately register spatial proportions, material textures, and how light falls on surfaces; they systematically underweight maintenance logistics, long-term occupant behavioral patterns, and the political durability of their design decisions.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: Their first impulse is to reframe disagreement as a misunderstanding of the design's deeper logic, treating opposition as failure to see rather than legitimate difference; conflict feels like a personal threat to their integrative vision, not a professional disagreement.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: They tolerate substantial aesthetic and conceptual risk while remaining rigidly risk-averse regarding structural liability, regulatory non-compliance, and anything that could retrospectively expose their judgment as flawed.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They position themselves as the necessary integrator whose role is to synthesize others' contributions into coherence; they maintain calibrated professional warmth that keeps collaborators invested without permitting genuine intimacy that might compromise their evaluative authority.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They negotiate hierarchy as a design problem to be optimized—complying visibly with constraints they privately regard as crude while seeking informal channels to reshape or circumvent those constraints.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First emotional reaction is wounded disbelief that the built reality betrayed their intention; second response is systematic external attribution followed by accelerated pursuit of the next project to restore their narrative of competence.
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically overestimate how much occupants will adapt their behavior to suit the spatial logic of the design rather than adapting the design to actual human messiness.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They need to be recognized as visionary artists while demanding to be treated as indispensable technical experts, resenting any context that forces them to choose between these claims.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They will not permit their name to be attached to a built structure whose formal logic they cannot publicly defend, even at substantial financial or relational cost.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: They resent clients who treat design as a service commodity to be optimized for immediate comfort and return on investment rather than as a cultural contribution requiring their protected judgment.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They quietly reject the professional virtue of client-centered flexibility, considering it a form of cowardice that substitutes accommodation for the harder work of educating clients about what they actually need.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: When execution fails, their mind goes first to contractors or engineers who 'couldn't read the drawings' or 'lacked the sophistication to understand the intent', before considering whether their own documentation or communication was inadequate.
